correctness.rationale: In the uniform Prüfer word, conditioning on d−1 marked labels leaves n−d−1 iid draws on the other n−1 labels, plus one marked leaf iff d=1. Prefix coupling gives the strict increasing order for d≥2, and adding one draw for d=1 can remove at most one empty box, with a repeat occurring with positive probability (strict comparison with d=2). The star law is the point mass n−1 and strictly dominates L1. At every interior d≥3, the lower endpoint is at least d, whereas L1=2 has positive mass; the upper endpoint is at most n−2, whereas L1=n−1 has positive mass. The two endpoint tails cross. With q=n−1 the degree-three difference is f(q)−1, f(q)=(2−1/q)(1−1/q)^(q−3). The displayed log derivative is negative already by log(1−1/q)≤−1/q. I checked f(7)=16848/16807>1 and f(8)=252105/262144<1. The d=4 expression is positive for q≥11 since (1−1/q)^(q−4)>e^(−1) and 3−3/q+1/q²≥331/121>e; direct exact checks for q=4..10 have smallest positive difference 44020511/100000000. Strict stochastic monotonicity then handles all d>4. Replay: /workspace/replays/recheck_frozen.py, leaves(), inclusion–exclusion tail checks at n=5..20 and exact boundary arithmetic. The analysis, not the bounded checks, handles all n.

value.rationale: A marked vertex's degree is a natural predictor for the global leaf count. The result turns the known degree-two valley into a complete set of comparisons and pinpoints a nontrivial all-size sign pattern for means: degree three switches at nine while the stochastic incomparability never changes, and degree four and above never switch. The useful distinction is between prediction in expectation and full tail order, not a new occupancy model or a census through an arbitrary n.
